# PR #5303: Patch: write the card data JSON one record per line, about 260k fewer lines

Closes #5289

## What changed

The card data JSON is now written one record per line: one card, one patch, one row or one voice-line entry per line. Only white space outside strings changes, so every file parses to the same value with the same key order. Ruling **R5289000** records the format (`spec/rulings/R5289000.md`, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/5289.md`).

- **One layout function.** `crates/tools/src/json_layout.rs` has `layout(json, depth)`. It works on the text from `serde_json::to_string`, so numbers, escapes and key order stay exactly as written. The rule:
  - A container above the record depth opens and closes on its own lines, one member per line, when it is the root and not empty, or when it holds an object or an array.
  - Every other container is written compact on its member's line. So a delta's `"unset"` and the report's `"filter"` stay on one line.
- **The depths.** `crates/tools/src/format_json.rs` names each depth as a constant (rule 9) and lists every file or folder with its depth in `LAYOUTS`:
  - 1: the catalog, the two sidecars, `patches.json`, `technical.json`, `index.json`, `card_metrics/` and each folder's `versions.json`.
  - 2: the deltas, `records/`, `win_rates/`, `dev-40.report.json` and the voice manifest.
- **Every writer uses it:**
  - `patches_io::write_records` and `js::stringify_records` in `patches.rs`: the deltas from ship and encode, `versions.json`, `patches.json` and `index.json` from `rebuild_derived`, ship and cut, the records table, and the card lists.
  - `retcon.rs`, `technical.rs` (`patches log`) and `stats.rs` (`stats report --json`, which writes `dev-40.report.json`).
  - The card-text export test that writes `flavour.json` and `chinese.json`.
  - `gen-voice.mjs`, through `apps/web/scripts/json-layout.mjs`, a line-for-line JavaScript copy whose test holds it to the Rust's bytes.
  - `catalog.rs` and `winrates.rs` are unchanged: the first writes no file in the table, the second writes a pending fragment.
- **A new command, `cargo jackioh format-json [--check] [--root <dir>]`.** Without `--check` it lays out any file that isn't in shape; this did the one-time rewrite, and it is how a hand edit of `catalog.json` gets fixed (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` row 2 now says so). With `--check` it names each misformatted file and fails.
- **The check that keeps it (rule 15).** A new scan in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`, `r5289000_format_json_check_passes_on_the_tree_and_fails_on_a_two_space_copy`:
  - it passes on the tree;
  - on a scratch copy with two-space versions of all 8 single files plus one table from each of the 4 folders, it fails and names exactly those 12 files.
- **The rewrite.** The 147 files the layout changes were rewritten by `format-json` only, not by hand. The other 186 of the 333 were already in shape: empty deltas and `versions.json` maps of strings.

## Line counts

Counted with `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 cat | wc -l` on the branch and `git archive origin/main | tar -xO | wc -l` on main. The issue's `xargs -0 wc -l | tail -1` prints only the total of the last batch `xargs` makes.

| | before (main 71fca1b822) | after |
|---|---|---|
| tracked lines | 2,796,458 | 2,533,138 (−263,320) |
| the 333 files in the issue's table | 284,015 | 19,883 |

`git diff --stat origin/main`: 165 files changed, 19,316 insertions, 282,636 deletions.

## Readers

None needed a change; every reader parses the files as JSON:
- `crates/cards/build.rs` uses serde and strips the catalog's white space.
- The tools use serde.
- `apps/web/scripts/github-releases.ts` and `gen-voice.mjs` use `JSON.parse`.
- `analysis/jackioh_records` uses `json.load` for the catalog; its `json.loads(line)` calls read the `.jsonl` game records.
- `analysis/tests/test_card_stats.py` uses `json.loads` on `dev-40.report.json`.
- `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` uses `JSON.parse`.
- The workflows go through `jq`: `releases.yml`'s `git show … patches.json`, `gather.yml`, and `patches-ship.yml`'s list of logged commits.
- `rehearse.sh` greps the server's `/api/catalog` response, not the file.

No workflow writes one of these files except through `cargo jackioh` (`promote-production.yml` runs `patches log`).

## Merges (mergiraf)

`.gitattributes` sends `catalog.json`, `chinese.json`, `flavour.json` and the other JSON through mergiraf. That driver runs only where it is registered, which is the night bot's worktrees. GitHub's conflict detection and a person's clone use git's line merge.

So two branches that change **different fields of the same card** now conflict on that card's line wherever mergiraf isn't registered. Before, they merged cleanly unless the fields were near each other. Two branches adding or changing different cards still merge.

Nothing changes for `patches ship`, `cut` or `log` on main. The files they write (deltas, `patches.json`, `index.json`, `technical.json`) are written only there, by the tools, and `crates/cards/patches/**` is marked `!merge`, so git's line merge applies to them as before.

## Tests and checks

Run in this pass:
- `format-json --check`, `catalog check`, `patches check`, `spec check` and `cargo fmt --check` all exit 0. Spec check: 2751 rulings, ok.
- `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts` exits 0: 24,552 passed, 0 failed, 52 ignored (the daily `#[ignore]` tests). All five `r5289000` tests are among them, and `apps/web/src/wire` was clean afterwards.
- `classify --base origin/main --claims` printed `classify: App` and exited 0: no card plays differently and no fragment is asked for.
- The 147 changed JSON files equal their `origin/main` copies under `jq -c` (the comparison printed nothing).
- After `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, the web tests `json-layout.test.ts` and `ci-scope.test.ts` pass (393 tests). `eslint` on the changed web files exits 0, and `gen-voice.mjs --check` prints `ok, 1908 files`.

From the previous run's notes, before the last merge from main (that merge brought in no Rust and no JSON):
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exited 0.
- `golden check` exited 0, and `fuzz --seeds 200` passed all 200.
- `stats report --json` reproduces `dev-40.report.json` byte for byte.
- The web typecheck passed.
- The web `--changed origin/main` run passed 492 of 493 files. The one failure, `FriendsButton.test.tsx` R3728001, was a 15-second timeout while clippy held the CPU, and it passes alone (36/36).

## Decisions the issue didn't settle

- **The PR classifies as `kind:app`, not `kind:internal`.** The issue asks for a change to `apps/web/scripts/gen-voice.mjs`, and `classify` counts anything under `apps/web/` as App. It also compares `crates/cards/patches/*.json` byte for byte. Making it read JSON white space as layout would be a separate ruling, and gen-voice would still make the PR App. The check that matters still holds: no fragment, no card.
- **Old table blobs.** `shipped.json`'s blobs for tables shipped before this change hash the old two-space text. Editing them would amend shipped entries, which R646 forbids. So the R646 test now accepts either the file's own bytes or its two-space form, through `table_blobs`, a test-only helper. A table with one row changed matches neither; a new test proves that.
- **Snapshot blobs.** `snapshot_text` stays two-space, as R5268000 names it, so the 288 snapshot blobs don't move.
- **Files left two-space:** `shipped.json`, `order.json`, `aliases.json`, the pending fragments and `voice-text.json`. None is in the issue's table.
- **A text layout rather than a serde `Formatter` or a parsed value.** A `Formatter` can't look ahead, which keeping `unset` on one line needs. A parsed value would lose key order (the workspace has no `preserve_order`) and would print `1.0` as `1`; `dev-40` holds 47 such numbers.
- **A command rather than a rewrite done only inside a test,** because `catalog.json` is edited by hand.
- **Two additions to `scripts/ci-scope.sh`** although the issue says to leave its mapping alone. CLAUDE.md requires a file that a test newly reads from outside its crate to be in the map. The acceptance scan now reads `dev-40.report.json` and `voice-manifest.json`, so both now turn on `rust_tools_wasm`, and `dev-40.report.json` is no longer skipped. No existing mapping changed, and `ci-scope.test.ts` has a row for each.
- **The ruling's line-count sentence** now uses the current base, 71fca1b822, to match this description.

## Worth a second look

- `table_blobs` and the relaxed R646 assertions in `patches.rs`.
- `json-layout.mjs` against `json_layout.rs`. `voice.yml` commits the manifest, so the two must give identical bytes; the JavaScript test runs the Rust's own cases and the committed manifest.
- Ship's `lists_text` now uses the new layout. Sharing a table file between versions (R5268001) compares bytes, so the old two-space text would have made every ship write a duplicate file.

## Why

The repository holds about 2.8M tracked lines. About 334k are JSON, and most of that is card data pretty-printed by `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, which gives every field, and every tag in an array, a line of its own. A delta that changes 317 cards takes 9,776 lines (`crates/cards/patches/deltas/v0.2.0.json`). Writing each **record** (a card, a patch row, a version row) as one compact line keeps diffs and merges at the level of one card, and makes a `grep` for a card id return its whole entry in one hit. In return the tree shrinks by roughly a tenth.

This changes how the files are formatted, not what they contain: every file must parse to the same `serde_json::Value` as before.

const INDENT: &str = "  ";
fn is_space(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, ' ' | '\n' | '\r' | '\t') }
fn is_mark(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, '{' | '}' | '[' | ']' | ',' | ':') }
fn opens(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "{" | "[") }
fn closes(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "}" | "]") }
/// Each mark, each string whole, each other literal; white space dropped.
fn tokens(json: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = json.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((start, c)) = chars.next() {
        if is_space(c) { continue; }
        let mut end = start + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '"' {
            let mut escaped = false;
            for (at, d) in chars.by_ref() {
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                if escaped { escaped = false } else if d == '\\' { escaped = true } else if d == '"' { break }
            }
        } else if !is_mark(c) {
            while let Some(&(at, d)) = chars.peek() {
                if is_space(d) || is_mark(d) || d == '"' { break; }
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                chars.next();
            }
        }
        tokens.push(&json[start..end]);
    }
    tokens
}
fn new_line(out: &mut String, level: usize) { out.push('\n'); out.push_str(&INDENT.repeat(level)); }
pub fn layout(json: &str, depth: usize) -> String {
    let tokens = tokens(json);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    let mut open: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
    for (at, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        let rest = &tokens[at + 1..];
        if opens(token) {
            let wraps = open.len() < depth
                && if open.is_empty() {
                    rest.first().is_some_and(|next| !closes(next))
                } else {
                    rest.iter().find(|t| opens(t) || closes(t)).is_some_and(|t| opens(t))
                };
            out.push_str(token);
            open.push(wraps);
            if wraps { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
        } else if closes(token) {
            if open.pop() == Some(true) { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
            out.push_str(token);
        } else {
            out.push_str(token);
            if open.last() == Some(&true) {
                match *token { "," => new_line(&mut out, open.len()), ":" => out.push(' '), _ => {} }
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('\n');
    out
}

const INDENT: &str = "  ";
fn is_space(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, ' ' | '\n' | '\r' | '\t') }
fn is_mark(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, '{' | '}' | '[' | ']' | ',' | ':') }
fn opens(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "{" | "[") }
fn closes(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "}" | "]") }
/// Each mark, each string whole, each other literal; white space dropped.
fn tokens(json: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = json.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((start, c)) = chars.next() {
        if is_space(c) { continue; }
        let mut end = start + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '"' {
            let mut escaped = false;
            for (at, d) in chars.by_ref() {
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                if escaped { escaped = false } else if d == '\\' { escaped = true } else if d == '"' { break }
            }
        } else if !is_mark(c) {
            while let Some(&(at, d)) = chars.peek() {
                if is_space(d) || is_mark(d) || d == '"' { break; }
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                chars.next();
            }
        }
        tokens.push(&json[start..end]);
    }
    tokens
}
fn new_line(out: &mut String, level: usize) { out.push('\n'); out.push_str(&INDENT.repeat(level)); }
pub fn layout(json: &str, depth: usize) -> String {
    let tokens = tokens(json);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    let mut open: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
    for (at, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        let rest = &tokens[at + 1..];
        if opens(token) {
            let wraps = open.len() < depth
                && if open.is_empty() {
                    rest.first().is_some_and(|next| !closes(next))
                } else {
                    rest.iter().find(|t| opens(t) || closes(t)).is_some_and(|t| opens(t))
                };
            out.push_str(token);
            open.push(wraps);
            if wraps { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
        } else if closes(token) {
            if open.pop() == Some(true) { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
            out.push_str(token);
        } else {
            out.push_str(token);
            if open.last() == Some(&true) {
                match *token { "," => new_line(&mut out, open.len()), ":" => out.push(' '), _ => {} }
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('\n');
    out
}
